article.title: Why Feature Importance Is Not a Customer Persona
article.why: Separate model explanation from actionable customer segmentation.

paragraphs.en:
Feature-importance tools such as SHAP are useful because they help analysts explain why a predictive model gives high or low scores. But a list of important features is not automatically a customer persona. The two concepts answer different questions. Feature importance explains prediction; a persona describes a recognizable group that can support communication or action.

Suppose a propensity model shows that recent hospital spending, health-food purchases, age, and family-related transactions are important. It is tempting to combine these signals and name a persona such as ‘health-conscious family caregivers.’ That label may sound plausible, but the model has not proved that these features belong to the same people. One feature may matter for one subgroup and another feature for a different subgroup. Global importance summarizes patterns across many observations.

Even local SHAP values require care. They can explain which variables pushed one customer’s prediction upward or downward, but they do not tell us whether thousands of similar customers form a stable, coherent segment. To build a persona, analysts should examine combinations of behavior at customer level and test whether the proposed group has enough size, internal consistency, stability over time, and business relevance.

Actionability is especially important. A segment can be statistically interesting but useless for marketing if there is no distinct message, channel, offer, or intervention that fits it. Conversely, a relatively simple segment may be valuable if it maps clearly to a customer need and can be identified before a campaign begins.

There is also a causal trap. A feature can be strongly associated with a prediction without being a lever that the company can change. Age may be highly predictive, for example, but it is not an intervention. Even behavior such as frequent medical spending may describe a customer’s situation rather than a reason that a campaign will work. Prediction should therefore be separated from the question of what action can change an outcome.

A practical workflow is to use SHAP for hypothesis generation rather than persona generation. First, identify important signals and interesting interactions. Second, inspect customer-level distributions and combinations. Third, propose candidate segments. Fourth, measure segment size, stability, distinctiveness, and response to past actions when data are available. Finally, translate only the strongest patterns into business language.

This approach prevents a common mistake: giving a human-sounding name to a statistical pattern too early. SHAP can tell us where to look. It cannot, by itself, tell us who the customer ‘is.’ A useful persona is an analytical interpretation supported by multiple pieces of evidence, not simply a renamed feature-importance chart.
paragraphs.zh:
SHAP 等特徵重要度工具能解釋預測模型為何給出高低分，但重要特徵清單並不會自動變成顧客 persona。兩者回答不同問題：feature importance 解釋預測，persona 則描述可被辨識、可用於溝通或施策的一群人。

假設 propensity model 顯示近期醫療支出、健康食品、年齡與家庭相關交易很重要，很容易把它們合併成「重視健康的家庭照護者」。但模型並沒有證明這些特徵集中在同一群人身上；不同特徵可能分別對不同 subgroup 重要。Global importance 只是跨大量樣本的摘要。

即使 local SHAP 能說明單一顧客哪些變數推高或壓低預測，也不能證明數千名相似顧客形成穩定一致的 segment。建立 persona 時，應檢查顧客層級的行為組合，並驗證規模、內部一致性、時間穩定性與商業相關性。

Actionability 特別重要。某群體統計上有趣，但若沒有適合它的訊息、渠道、優惠或 intervention，對行銷可能沒有價值。反之，簡單 segment 若能清楚對應顧客需求且可在 campaign 前辨識，反而很實用。

還有因果陷阱：特徵與預測高度相關，不代表它是企業能改變的 lever。年齡可能很有預測力，但不是 intervention；醫療消費也可能只是描述狀態，而不是 campaign 有效的原因。

實務上可把 SHAP 當作 hypothesis generation：先找重要訊號與 interaction，再看顧客層級分布與組合，提出候選 segment，驗證規模、穩定性、區辨度與歷史施策反應，最後才把強而穩定的模式翻譯成商業語言。SHAP 告訴我們去哪裡看，但不能單獨告訴我們顧客「是誰」。
paragraphs.ja:
SHAPなどのfeature importanceは、予測modelがなぜ高低のscoreを出したかを説明するのに有効ですが、重要特徴量の一覧がそのままpersonaになるわけではありません。importanceは予測を説明し、personaは施策やcommunicationに使える認識可能な顧客群を表します。

例えば医療支出、健康食品、年齢、家族関連取引が重要でも、それらをまとめて「健康意識の高い家族介護層」と呼ぶのは早計です。各特徴が同じ顧客群に集中しているとは限らず、別々のsubgroupで効いている可能性があります。global importanceは多数の観測を横断した要約です。

local SHAPも、一人の予測を押し上げた変数は説明できますが、似た顧客が安定したsegmentを形成することまでは保証しません。persona化にはcustomer-levelの行動組合せ、規模、内部一貫性、時間的安定性、business relevanceの確認が必要です。

特にactionabilityが重要です。統計的に面白くても、固有のmessage、channel、offer、interventionにつながらなければmarketingでは使いにくい。一方、単純なsegmentでも顧客needsに結び付き、campaign前に識別できれば価値があります。

また、予測力と因果的leverを混同してはいけません。年齢は予測に効いても企業が変えられる変数ではありません。医療利用も状況を記述するだけで、campaignが効く理由とは限りません。

実務ではSHAPをpersona生成ではなくhypothesis generationに使います。重要signalとinteractionを見つけ、顧客単位の分布と組合せを確認し、候補segmentを作り、規模・安定性・distinctiveness・過去施策への反応を検証してからbusiness languageへ翻訳します。SHAPは「どこを見るか」を示しますが、「顧客が誰か」を単独で決めるものではありません。

vocabulary.usage: Check whether the segment is coherent.
A predictive feature is not always an intervention.
A plausible label can still be wrong.
Features may matter for different subgroups.
Prediction does not identify a causal lever.

business.term: SHAP should generate hypotheses, not personas by itself.
business.explanation: 說明模型解釋與 persona 設計的界線。

business.term: We need to validate size, stability, and actionability before naming the segment.
business.explanation: persona 命名前的實務檢查。
